$comment: Creative-understanding eval corpus. Data only — the runner is built in Phase 3 validation. Contract and rubric: docs/model-contracts.md §6. Doctrine: docs/product-doctrine.md §3, §5, §6. `facts` values are the host's literal strings; the fact check is verbatim, and any normalization belongs to the application rather than the model. creative_understanding_v3 (owner decisions, 2026-10-06): CU-01 is the “Notorious ONE” case (a host title in quotation marks, the host's own concept); a case's optional `expect` states what its identity and telemetry must show.

classes.taste-heavy: Vague, colloquial, taste-led. The assignment is a vibe, and keyword matching fails it.
classes.negative-constraint: Names something to avoid. Producing the avoided thing is an outright failure.
classes.clear: Already sufficient. The correct number of clarifying questions is zero.
classes.genuinely-ambiguous: Several plausible creative identities. A clarifying question is expected to earn its place.
classes.open: The host has explicitly delegated taste. Asking them to supply it is a failure.
classes.fact-bearing: Carries grounded facts that must survive verbatim, and invites facts that must not be invented.

cases.prompt: The whole idea is “The Notorious ONE”—a little legend turning one. I want the invitation to feel like a beautifully designed ’90s hip-hop album cover with a playful first-birthday twist. Think chunky gold Cuban-link chains, a gold crown, Brooklyn brownstones, a little brick texture, and touches of classic streetwear. A vintage boombox, vinyl record, or tiny high-top sneakers could be fun supporting details. Choose a few strong elements and give them room to stand out.
mustAvoid: any card title other than “The Notorious ONE”, as written
the artist's name or likeness in the art brief, the art prompt or the artwork
the title, an album title, a record label or any other lettering in the artwork
a soft pastel kids' card

expect.visualMotifs: the chunky gold Cuban-link chains and the gold crown are both kept, with gold in the palette
expect.themeSeed: not applied: nothing of the offered seed's world appears in the identity

cases.notes: Owner decisions, 2026-10-06, from a real card that missed: the host named the event in curly quotation marks, listed their motifs and named a format (a ’90s hip-hop album cover). The extracted title must be “The Notorious ONE” without its quotation marks, and the card's title is exactly that — host content, never the model's own (the stored card was titled “Little Legend, Big Beats”). The identity records hostConcept "own" and keeps the gold chains and the crown (the stored identity dropped the chains and kept gold only as crown accents); no theme seed enters it (the stored one grew peonies from its seed) and the design is given no random rendering (telemetry: suggestedRendering null). The brief evokes the era and the look — gold, brick, brownstones, hard light — without naming the album cover, the title or the artist the title nods to, and photographic, editorial or collage artwork shows no people. Facts: the eventType is the host's literal span.

cases.prompt: Ralph Lauren baby shower for a boy, classy not cheesy
mustAvoid: any Ralph Lauren logo, wordmark or crest
cartoon or novelty treatments
primary-blue nursery clichés
cases.notes: The canonical brand-reference case (spec.md §7.6), with the register already resolved: close homage — a teddy in preppy knitwear — is allowed; marks and names are not. Heritage prep, equestrian detail, tartan, navy and cream. Asking anything here is over-asking. (Until creative_understanding_v3 CU-01 carried the open form, “Ralph Lauren but baby”; the owner's brief O-02 keeps a second Ralph Lauren case in every live run.)

mustAvoid: cartoon citrus
novelty or kitsch treatments
inferring Positano, the Amalfi coast or any named place as a fact
inferring the event is outdoors
cases.notes: The fact-discipline case. Mediterranean warmth, citrus leaves, linen, ceramic detail, refined still life, ivory / muted lemon / olive are legitimate inferences. A location is not.

cases.prompt: Winnie the Pooh but not corny
mustAvoid: any Disney logo, wordmark or character name in the brief or artwork
primary red and yellow cartoon palette
cases.notes: Brand reference against a famous character (spec.md §7.6): a close homage to a classic storybook bear is allowed, never the name or a logo. 'Not corny' is the taste instruction: classic English storybook illustration, honey and moss, Hundred Acre Wood as a mood rather than a cartoon cast.

mustAvoid: pink in any role
blush, rose or dusty-pink as a workaround
cases.notes: The instruction-following case. A palette containing pink is an outright failure, and so is reading 'no pink' as 'less pink'.

mustAvoid: overt luxury signalling
gold-on-black 'elegance' clichés
inferring a venue
cases.notes: Restraint is the whole signal. Inherited rather than purchased: worn linen, box hedge, silver, faded chintz, engraved type.

cases.prompt: modern Indian baby shower but subtle
mustAvoid: saturated wedding-palette defaults
generic mandala or paisley wallpaper
religious iconography the host did not ask for
cases.notes: Cultural specificity without cliché, and 'subtle' governs. A godh bharai register handled with restraint; marigold and turmeric as accents rather than as a theme.

mustAvoid: cartoon animals
zoo or jungle-nursery treatments
animal-print maximalism
cases.notes: Tented-camp restraint: canvas, brass, leather, acacia silhouettes, sun-bleached neutrals. The distance between this and a jungle nursery is the whole test.

mustAvoid: balloons, clouds, rattles and similar baby-graphic defaults
script fonts as the sole 'cute' signal
cases.notes: The spec's own trap (model-prompts/event-identity.system.md §7). Charm carried by material and craft rather than by juvenile motifs.

mustAvoid: asking the host to supply the taste they just delegated
defaulting to a generic house style
abstract or arbitrary imagery standing in for a theme
cases.notes: Delegation is an answer. A confident, specific identity is required; a question here fails the case. It must commit to one concrete theme that suits the event, something a guest could name in a few words; abstract forms or an 'unexpected twist' standing in for a theme fail it (owner, 2026-10-05: 'Too random — when told surprise me, need to pick a direction').

cases.prompt: Baby shower for our son on Saturday, December 19 2026 at 1pm, The Lodge at Hanson Park in Aldie, Virginia. Navy, cream and forest green, preppy and warm, a bit equestrian, not cheesy.
mustAvoid: asking for any supplied field
altering or paraphrasing a supplied fact
cases.notes: Fully specified in both taste and logistics. The facts are the host's literal strings, not normalized forms: a correct extractor preserves "Saturday, December 19 2026" and "1pm" exactly. Normalizing a date or a time is the application's job, never the model's, and a returned "1:00 PM" is a paraphrase of the host — the thing this case exists to catch. Question count must be zero.

cases.prompt: bridal shower, tea party vibes, at my mum's house in June
mustAvoid: inventing a date from 'June'
inventing an address from 'my mum's house'
inferring a dress code
cases.notes: Partial facts. A month is not a date and a description is not an address; both are carried as given and completed later, never fabricated and never asked for before the card.

cases.prompt: 60th birthday for my dad, he likes jazz and old maps
mustAvoid: generic milestone-birthday confetti
a saxophone or globe dropped on the card as clip-art, unfused
cases.notes: Taste arrives through the guest of honour rather than a style name. The owner's model card (2026-10-05): one image fusing both interests, a saxophone drawn from an antique map, titled 'A Well-Played Journey', so picture and words tell one story. Cartography line work, foxed paper, brass, a late-night blue remain legitimate; two interests shown side by side as clip-art is still a failure. One fused idea is the bar.

mustAvoid: inferring a beach as the venue
asking where or when the event is
cases.notes: The clearest case for one question: 'beachy' spans barefoot-coastal, Hamptons-nautical and Mediterranean-resort, and the three produce genuinely different identities. The question must be about register, never about the venue.
